alloy.preparation: Alloy-design specimen, nominal 27.5% Cr–3.8% Mo with 6–8% Ni; simulated heat-affected zone subjected to the Figure 2 thermal cycle: peak 1648 K for 1 s, cooling at 30 K/s. The manufacturing route of the subsequently developed P/M tube is not automatically assigned to these alloy-design specimens.
alloy.microstructure: Duplex stainless-steel alloy-design series. The source associates low-Ni HAZ degradation with Cr carbonitride precipitation and high-Ni degradation with sigma precipitation; the individual markers are not assigned a particular precipitate state.

test_solution.preparation: Synthetic seawater as named by the source; recipe, pH and gas conditioning not supplied. Natural seawater immersion and NaCl crevice tests are separate experiments.

test_method.procedure_description: Pitting potential measured by potential-sweep polarization; values reported vs SCE. Figure 4 simulated HAZ at 353 K, 20 mV/min.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Reported pitting potential Vc-prime; no general numerical current criterion is stated. Upward arrows remain lower testing bounds, not observed thresholds.

experiments.result_note: Approximate graphical reading. Individual Ni contents are not supplied for the markers; no series identity is invented. Ni 6–8% is the reported range across this Figure 4 specimen set, not an individually resolved Ni analysis. Nitrogen is the approximate registered graphical coordinate.

alloy.preparation: 28Cr seamless tube produced by nitrogen-gas atomization of duplex-steel powder; packed in a mild-steel capsule, cold isostatically pressed and hot extruded; capsule removed by acid pickling, then heat treated at 1373 K (1100 °C) and water quenched. Subsequently heat treated for 10 s at maximum temperature 1373 K for the Figure 10 comparison.
alloy.microstructure: Ferritic–austenitic duplex stainless steel. Ferrite fraction depends on the thermal treatment; no value is inferred from a different state. The text and plot differ on the exact high-temperature ferrite fraction of 28Cr, so none is imposed.

test_solution.preparation: Synthetic seawater as named by the source; recipe, pH and gas conditioning not supplied. Natural seawater immersion and NaCl crevice tests are separate experiments.

test_method.procedure_description: Pitting potential measured by potential-sweep polarization; values reported vs SCE. For the heat-treatment/weld figures the source does not restate a numerical electrolyte temperature or scan rate; those fields remain null.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Reported pitting potential Vc-prime; no general numerical current criterion is stated. Upward arrows remain lower testing bounds, not observed thresholds.

experiments.result_note: Upward limit arrow at 1.0 V. The maximum heating temperature or welding heat input is a specimen-treatment variable, not electrolyte temperature. A numerical test temperature is not explicitly supplied for this figure.
